newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Truckers union threatens new protests.
newsitem.headline: French Truckers union threatens new protests.

text.p: The giant Force Ouvriere (FO) union on Sunday threatened new protests by French truckers, accusing the government of failing to keep the promises it made to settle a crippling 12-day strike in November.
"I sense that we are going to have to issue a new appeal to truckers to again bring their vehicles out on the roads," FO secretary-general Roger Poletti said on France Info radio.
Truckers shut down numerous highways across the country in mid-November by abandoning their vehicles in the middle of key routes and erecting hundreds of roadblocks.
They also blocked access to petrol depots, creating an artificial scarcity of petrol and forcing some cities and towns to restrict sales in order to keep emergency vehicles in service.

Despite a government austerity plan to help France qualify for European monetary union, the truckers were able to extract pledges from the government and transport firms for retirement at 55 instead of 60, higher pay, a cash bonus, compulsory rest time and payment during loading and standby time.
But Poletti said the promises had not been kept.
He said eligibility requirements for earlier retirement were too rigid, no bonuses had been paid and rest-time rules had never been issued.
"The government has decided to decide nothing," he said.
The threat of fresh trucker protests is a new challenge to government hopes to keep down public deficits in order to help France qualify for a single European currency from 1999.
Public spending has been cut and some taxes increased despite record 12.7 percent unemployment.
Other unions, encouraged by the concessions won by the truckers, have been scrambling to stage their own protests and strikes, hinting at the possibility of a new period of labour unrest in France.
Six trade unions seeking retirement at 55 have called for a nationwide strike in the public transport sector for January 24.

And train drivers in the CFDT union have appealed for a nationwide rail strike on January 31 in protest at government plans to overhaul the state-owned SNCF rail authority, a project the union fears could lead to job losses.

Memories are still vivid in France of a late 1995 strike by railway and other public transport workers which paralysed the country for more than three weeks just ahead of the Christmas holiday season.
